source_text: Among groups such as the Dogon or Mandinka, the procedure—often termed sunna for partial clitoral removal—was executed post-menarche using non-sterile tools like knives or thorns, justified by beliefs in enhancing marital fidelity or averting infertility through genital "purification." [23] [16]
